Partial Pre-Integration is a cell projection technique that improves ray integration approximation in volume rendering by utilizing a 2D lookup table ($\psi$ table) that is independent of the transfer function [S1].

The claim states that Partial Pre-Integration is a cell projection technique improving ray integration approximation using a 2D lookup table ($ψ$ table) independent of the transfer function. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly confirms that the partial pre-integration approach computes a table independent of the transfer function to overcome the disadvantage of recomputation. It details that RGBA colors are retrieved from the transfer function to compute indices into this 2D ψ table, which is then used to compute the final fragment color (improving approximation by being less prone to under-sampling errors). The evidence supports all specific facts mentioned in the claim.
supported
*   **Transfer Function Changes:** Unlike Full Pre-Integration, the $\psi$ table does not need to be recomputed when the transfer function changes [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the partial pre-integration approach computes a table (the 2D ψ table) which is 'independent of the transfer function' and 'does not depend on any attribute of the visualization'. It contrasts this with full pre-integration, where 'every time it [the transfer function] changes the table must be recomputed.' Furthermore, it notes that with partial pre-integration, 'we are able to change the transfer function interactively,' implying the table does not need recomputation, only reloading of the lookup texture which has 'very little overhead.' This directly supports the claim that the ψ table does not need to be recomputed when the transfer function changes.
supported
